checks: Each live primary PDF was inspected once. The local SHA-256 matched both papers.primary_file_sha256 and paper_files.file_sha256 for S1247, S1260, S1384 and S1903.

S1899's previously cached PDF did not match the live attachment and was not used. The actual live PDF was downloaded once from papers storage, SHA-256 matched papers.primary_file_sha256 and paper_files.file_sha256, and that file was inspected.

Population layouts were selected before staging: Total / LEA / MEA / OEA (S1247); Baseline / 12-month follow-up (S1260); Second division total / Second division female / Second division male (S1384); no extraction populations for S1899 or S1903.

Tabs 1-4 were staged for every schema-compatible player cohort. All tables and usable figures were swept once for the compatible psychiatric/psychological outcome fields; injury fields were not populated from historical or association-only injury information.

S1247 and S1260 report overlapping mental-health symptoms, so no artificial all-illness total was created. Their direct psychiatric/metabolic structured rows preserve the compatible condition-specific counts and percentages.

S1899 is a referee cohort, so it is correctly routed to referee rather than player extraction. S1903 is an academy screening-tool development and psychometric-validation study with no reportable disorder prevalence or injury/illness surveillance payload, so it remains mental_health.

All staged field IDs were validated against the live extraction schema. No exposure, injury count, or population value was derived from an incompatible denominator. S1247's two n≈11 psychiatric counts are transparent nearest-whole conversions from 44% of the directly reported 25-player denominator.

sourceCoverage.S1247: Primary PDF pp. 1-9: abstract, methods/definitions, Tables 1-5, Figures 1-3, results, discussion, limitations and conclusion. No reportable injury surveillance outcome; Figure 3 supplied direct mental-health percentages.
sourceCoverage.S1260: Primary PDF pp. 1-8: abstract, methods/validated questionnaire definitions, Tables 1-4, results, discussion, limitations and conclusion. The online supplement was referenced but not attached; it was not required for the reported Table 2 values.
sourceCoverage.S1384: Primary PDF pp. 1-14: abstract, participant/design methods, Tables 1-4, results, discussion, limitations and conclusion. MINI diagnostic outcomes are reported only for the second-division comparison cohort.
sourceCoverage.S1899: Live primary PDF pp. 199-214: abstract, methods, Tables 1-4, results, discussion, limitations and conclusion. It exclusively studies Turkish amateur football referees.
sourceCoverage.S1903: Primary PDF pp. 33-45: abstract, three development/validation phases, participant section, psychometric results, discussion, limitations and Appendix A. It reports tool validity/reliability, not extractable disorder prevalence.

studyDetails.title: Risk for low energy availability, disordered eating and sleep disturbance among female football players

definitions.illnessDefinition: SMHAT-1 step-1 poor mental-health screen and step-2 symptom-specific cutoffs
definitions.incidenceDefinition: prevalence at a single precompetition assessment (percent of players)

caveats: Total / LEA / MEA / OEA follows the directly reported energy-availability strata. Mental-health and low-energy-availability values are pooled only, so their values stay on the Total line.

The psychiatric count n=11 is a transparent nearest-whole conversion of the direct 44% value over 25 players. The study's poor-mental-health and disordered-eating percentages overlap, so no all-illness total is asserted.
The 8% injury-history item is a LEAF-Q history item in a study that excluded current musculoskeletal injury; it is not an injury-surveillance outcome and was not mapped.

studyDetails.title: Don't forget to mind the mind: a prospective cohort study over 12 months on mental health symptoms in active professional male footballers
studyDetails.journal: BMC Sports Science, Medicine and Rehabilitation

participantCharacteristics.levelOfPlay: professional first- or second-tier national league

definitions.illnessDefinition: mental-health symptoms meeting validated APSQ, GAD-7, PHQ-9, BEDA-Q, ASSQ, AUDIT-C or CAGE-AID cutoffs
definitions.incidenceDefinition: baseline prevalence and 12-month new-symptom incidence using symptom-specific denominators

caveats: Baseline / 12-month follow-up is the strongest direct reporting axis. The 12-month incidence denominators differ by symptom because only players free from that symptom at baseline are eligible; the 80-person response count is retained only as the follow-up cohort size.
Distress is the most frequent reported symptom at both time points. Mental-health symptom categories overlap, so no all-illness total, injury total, or aggregate rate was created.
Tables 3-4 report historical/association injury and surgery data without a prospective injury-surveillance denominator; no injury fields were populated.

studyDetails.title: Mental Health in First- and Second-Division Soccer Players: A Cross-Sectional Study

definitions.illnessDefinition: MINI structured diagnostic interview for DSM-IV and ICD-10 psychiatric disorders
definitions.incidenceDefinition: prevalence among second-division players at a single cross-sectional assessment

caveats: The direct diagnostic table only covers the 42 second-division players. First-division men were assessed with other scales but did not receive the MINI diagnostic interview, so no all-54 diagnosis total was inferred.

Second division total / female / male preserves the table's overlapping total-and-subgroup layout. Total MINI diagnosis represents players with one or more diagnoses; category counts are comorbid and were not summed.
No injury or exposure surveillance data are reported.
